region.name: Wildcat Ridge, Hawksbill Gap, western Jezero delta
region.geographic_coordinates: Planetocentric latitude and east-positive longitude in degrees

elevation.unit: meters above the product's MOLA-derived delta geoid

science.kind: In situ elemental and mineralogical measurements
science.site: Berry Hollow abrasion patch, Wildcat Ridge

published_observation.reference: Figures 2 and 5 of Jones et al. (2025)
published_observation.result: PIXL diffraction identified anhydrite and gypsum in the Berry Hollow vein. The study reports approximately 45 percent anhydrite and 37 percent gypsum among the calcium-sulfate dehydration phases for BH2.
published_observation.limitation: These percentages describe the study's analysis of the BH2 scan. They do not describe the bulk rock, surrounding terrain, or the full crop.

science.coverage: Centimeter-scale abrasion patch; display as point evidence. The Sol 502 rover position locates the workspace approximately and does not give the instrument footprint.
science.rationale: Investigate nearby fine-grained sedimentary rocks for evidence of how water interacted with the ancient delta. PIXL identified calcium sulfate phases in the Berry Hollow veins; the measured phases apply to that patch.
